rules.title: Source of lawful income discrimination prohibited (NJ Law Against Discrimination)
rules.requirement: A New Jersey landlord cannot refuse to rent to you, or treat you differently, because of your lawful source of income or rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher. You may file a free complaint with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or sue in Superior Court within two years.

coverage.summary: Applies to the rental of all property statewide, except an apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling, rooms rented by the owner or occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, and religious-organization preferences.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Rooms rented in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
Religious organization preference for persons of the same religion

rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner or occupant; religious-organization preferences for persons of the same religion.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.

notes: Division on Civil Rights brochure (rev. 2015) summarizing the NJ LAD. The document does not give the codified section for the source-of-income provision, so none is cited. Other LAD protections it describes (protected classes, disability accommodations) fall outside the six categories. The brochure does not cover criminal-history screening.
